title: Ricci/Weyl orthogonal decomposition of an algebraic curvature tensor
expression_sketch: Algebraic curvature tensor R_ijkl on an n-dimensional pseudo-Riemannian space with nondegenerate metric g, n=4 in the displayed coefficients. Traceless Ricci: Z_jk = Ric_jk - (1/n)*Scal*g_jk.  Scalar, traceless-Ricci, and Weyl pieces (Wikipedia Ricci decomposition, that page's Riemann sign convention): S_ijkl = Scal/(n*(n-1)) * (g_il*g_jk - g_ik*g_jl), E_ijkl = 1/(n-2) * (Z_il*g_jk - Z_jl*g_ik - Z_ik*g_jl + Z_jk*g_il), W_ijkl = R_ijkl - S_ijkl - E_ijkl.  For n=4: S = Scal/12 * (g_il g_jk - g_ik g_jl), E uses 1/2.  Reconstruction: R = S+E+W.  Orthogonality: <S,E>=<S,W>=<E,W>=0 and |R|^2 = |S|^2+|E|^2+|W|^2 with index raising by g.  W is totally traceless: g^{il} W_ijkl = 0.  Each of S,E,W inherits Riemann symmetries including the Bianchi cycle.
latent_structure: Symmetry-adapted O(g)-irreducible splitting of the algebraic curvature space: RV = SV ⊕ EV ⊕ CV (scalar ⊕ traceless-Ricci ⊕ Weyl) via Kulkarni-Nomizu products with g. Invariant orthogonal projectors, not a relabeling of Riemann indices.

function_domains.g: Nondegenerate symmetric metric of any signature on an n-dimensional vector space (cotangent model).
function_domains.R: Algebraic curvature tensor: skew in 12 and 34, pair symmetry 12<->34, Bianchi identity; Wikipedia sign convention R_ijkl = g_lp (d_i Gamma_jk^p - d_j Gamma_ik^p + ...).
function_domains.Ric: Ricci tensor R_jk = g^{il} R_ijkl with the contraction of that page.
function_domains.W: Weyl tensor, the totally traceless piece.

nonzero_conditions.statement: n=4, hence n != 0, n-1 != 0, n-2 != 0, so the displayed denominators n(n-1) and n-2 are invertible in Q.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Ricci decomposition: n-manifold; irreducible split stated for n >= 4

nonzero_conditions.statement: g is nondegenerate, so g^{ij} exists and is used to raise indices and form traces.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED

branch_conventions: No square roots: the volume-form Levi-Civita tensor is not used. Index raising uses g^{-1} only.
source_provenance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weyl_tensor (component formula; Ricci decomposition as O(n) irreps)
Besse, Einstein Manifolds, Ergebnisse 10, Springer 1987, Chapter 1 §G.
Singer and Thorpe, The curvature of 4-dimensional Einstein spaces, 1969.
Wald, General Relativity, Chicago 1984, p. 40 (physics Weyl formula).

derived_conditions.statement: The Wikipedia Ricci-decomposition page uses the less common Ricci-sign convention (contract first and last index of that Riemann); the S,E,W formulae are tied to that choice.
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Wikipedia Ricci decomposition, definition section note on sign convention

derived_conditions.statement: S,E,W each have Riemann algebraic symmetries because they are Kulkarni-Nomizu products (or the complementary Weyl remainder).
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Wikipedia Ricci decomposition, properties of the pieces

derived_conditions.statement: Orthogonality <S,E>=<S,W>=<E,W>=0 is with respect to the metric-induced inner product on (0,4) tensors.
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Wikipedia Ricci decomposition, properties of the decomposition

derived_conditions.statement: n=4 is a specialization of the general-n formulae; coefficients 1/12 and 1/2 are n(n-1)=12 and n-2=2.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

public_source: Wikipedia Ricci decomposition and Weyl tensor; Besse 1987; Singer-Thorpe 1969
why_not_cse_lgg: An expanded Riemann array with 20 independent 4D components does not CSE into Weyl plus Ricci plus scalar. LGG cannot invent the Kulkarni-Nomizu product or the O(n) irrep projectors. The target is a change of representation on the curvature module.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide Weyl, Schouten, Kulkarni-Nomizu, Ricci decomposition, conformal. Do not give the 1/(n-2) template in scientific_context.
notes: Pointwise algebraic identity on curvature tensors; no PDE, no analytic continuation, no coordinate-chart assumption beyond a nondegenerate metric. n=4 is declared (GR/4-manifold case). Physical reading (gravitational waves vs matter) is not required for the tensor identity.
